Companion Animal Travel Desk: Booking and Care Rules

This section explains how the Companion Animal Travel Desk handles animal travel requests, checks, and handoff steps for Aurelia Skyways.

Staff should keep the booking file complete, clear, and easy to follow from first contact through final confirmation. <<FACT F091>> The traveler record should include the animal's basic details, carrier notes, and any handling concerns that affect the trip. Keep language simple when speaking with travelers so they know what to bring, how to prepare, and when to arrive at the desk.

The staff role responsible for booking oversight must review each case before it moves forward. <<FACT F097>> If a traveler arrives with missing documents, pause the process and explain what is needed before the file can continue. When a pet is accepted, note the carrier condition, label the file plainly, and share the handling summary with the cabin team so the animal is watched properly during flight. If the traveler changes plans, update the file at once so the desk, gate team, and cabin team stay aligned. Mochi, if listed on a trip, should be treated like any other approved pet and handled with the same calm, careful approach. Isaac Fischer and Nikhil Ramos may be used as sample traveler names in training only, but real files should always follow the actual booking record.

Keep the tone steady and respectful at all times, because travelers often worry about their animals and need clear guidance. Do not promise exceptions, do not guess about approvals, and do not leave details for later if they affect safe transport. If a concern comes up during check-in or in the cabin, pass it to the lead coordinator right away and record what was done.

For help with any booking issue, contact the lead coordinator or the station manager through the normal desk channel.
